# LLM Guard (content-guardrail engine) — deploy configs

The console's guardrail port (`src/lib/adapters/pii.ts`, sole engine, fail-closed) talks to an
LLM Guard API over `OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_URL` (POST `/analyze/prompt`, bearer `_API_KEY`).

## Configs
- **`scanners-full.yml`** — the FULL scanner suite in ONE container (Anonymize/PII, PromptInjection,
  BanTopics, Toxicity, Gibberish, Language, BanCompetitors, Secrets, Regex, InvisibleText + output
  scanners). **`use_onnx: false` on every transformer scanner is REQUIRED** — the archived
  `laiyer/llm-guard-api` image references ONNX model files (e.g.
  `ProtectAI/deberta-v3-base-prompt-injection-v2 onnx/model.onnx`) that 404 at their pinned HF
  revisions; PyTorch weights load fine. Needs ~5–6 GB — OOMs a 7.8 GB VM, so we shard instead (below).
- **`scanners-pii.yml`** — the PII/DLP shard: Anonymize + Secrets + Regex + BanSubstrings +
  InvisibleText (~1.9 GB). Runs on S1.
- **`scanners-classifiers.yml`** — the heavy-classifier shard: PromptInjection + Toxicity + Gibberish
  + Language (~4.3 GB). Runs on S2. Together with the PII shard + the aggregator this is the full
  suite, split to fit the VM cap (see SHARDED topology below).

## Run (headless OrbStack, e.g. on S2 / the aux box)
    docker run -d --name llm-guard --restart unless-stopped -p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000 \
      -e AUTH_TOKEN=<token> -e LOG_LEVEL=INFO \
      -v $PWD/scanners-full.yml:/home/user/app/config/scanners.yml:ro \
      laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16
    # then on the console host: OFFGRID_ADAPTER_GUARDRAILS=llm-guard,
    # OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 (loopback fwd to the guard host),
    # OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_API_KEY=<token>; restart the console.

## Capacity note (2026-07-12)
The FULL suite needs ~5–6 GB in the container. The fleet's OrbStack VMs are capped at 7.8 GB and
already run the data/control containers, so the full suite OOMs in ONE container. Raising the
OrbStack VM memory (`orb config set memory_mib …` did NOT apply over SSH — needs the OrbStack app's
memory GUI) was the original unblock, but the cleaner one is **sharding** (below).

## SHARDED topology (2026-07-12, LIVE) — the full suite without raising VM memory
Instead of one fat container, the scanner suite is **split across fleet nodes**, each shard fitting
its own 7.8 GB VM, with a fan-out **aggregator** in front so the console still talks to ONE endpoint.

    console  ──POST /analyze/prompt──▶  guardrail-aggregator (S1, 127.0.0.1:8010, root LaunchDaemon)
                                          ├─▶ pii shard         (S1  127.0.0.1:8000)  scanners-pii.yml         [required]
                                          └─▶ classifiers shard (S2  offgrid-s2.local:8000) scanners-classifiers.yml [optional]

- **`scripts/guardrail-aggregator.mjs`** (S1) fans the prompt to both shards and merges the verdicts
  (pure merge in `scripts/lib/guard-merge.mjs`, unit-tested). It runs as a **root** LaunchDaemon
  (`/Library/LaunchDaemons/co.getoffgridai.guard-aggregator.plist`) — root reaches the LAN
  (`offgrid-s2.local`); a user LaunchAgent is blocked by macOS Local Network privacy, exactly like
  the gateway aggregator. Caddy is the public edge; the internal fleet fan-out is the aggregator's job.
- **Fail-closed vs degrade:** the on-box PII shard is REQUIRED (down → the aggregator 502s → the
  console blocks the run). The S2 classifier shard is OPTIONAL — if S2 hiccups, the verdict stands on
  the PII shard and the response carries `x-offgrid-guard-degraded: classifiers`, so a flaky aux node
  never takes governed runs offline. `GET /health` on :8010 shows per-shard state.

### Bring up / restart a shard
    # classifiers shard on S2 (LAN-bound, token-protected like the gateways; --memory caps a crash):
    docker run -d --name llm-guard-classifiers --restart unless-stopped --memory 6g \
      -p 0.0.0.0:8000:8000 -e AUTH_TOKEN=<token> -e LOG_LEVEL=INFO \
      -v /tmp/scanners-classifiers.yml:/home/user/app/config/scanners.yml:ro laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16
    # NB: `--restart unless-stopped` reuses the container on reboot so the downloaded HF models
    # persist; only a `docker rm` re-downloads (~4 min — no HF cache volume is mounted).

### Console wiring (on the box .env.local — NOT git)
    OFFGRID_ADAPTER_GUARDRAILS=llm-guard
    OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8010   # the aggregator, not a shard
    OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_API_KEY=<token>             # = the aggregator's OFFGRID_GUARD_AGGREGATOR_TOKEN

To add a THIRD shard (e.g. BanTopics/NoRefusal/BanCompetitors on another node), append it to the
daemon's `OFFGRID_GUARD_SHARDS` JSON with its own `OFFGRID_GUARD_TOKEN_<NAME>` and kickstart the
aggregator — no console change.

# Off Grid — File Storage API

Upload files, retrieve them, and toggle public/private. Files are stored **on-prem**
(local disk on the server; metadata in Postgres) — nothing leaves your infrastructure.

- **Base URL:** `https://gateway.getoffgridai.co`
- **Auth (write/list/manage):** the unified **key flow** — a Keycloak **service-account
  JWT** as `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (the same key model as the gateway). A console
  login session (cookie) also works for humans.
- **Public reads:** no auth. Private reads: require the Bearer key (else `404`).

### Getting a key (service account)
Keycloak issues machine keys — we don't run a custom key store. Create a service-account
client (Console → **Access → Machine Clients**, or reuse an existing one), then exchange
its `client_id`/`client_secret` for a short-lived JWT:
```bash
API_KEY=$(curl -s https://<keycloak>/realms/offgrid/protocol/openid-connect/token \
  -d grant_type=client_credentials -d client_id=<your-client> -d client_secret=<secret> \
  | jq -r .access_token)
```
Re-mint when it expires (~5 min). To manage files owned by others / act as admin, give
the service account the `admin` realm role in Keycloak; otherwise it manages its own.

> Private files return **404** (not 403) to callers without access, so their existence
> isn't revealed.

---

## Upload — `POST /api/v1/files`

Query: `?visibility=public|private` (default `private`). Two body styles:

**Raw bytes** (set the filename + type via headers):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files?visibility=private" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Filename: report.pdf" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/pdf" \
  --data-binary @report.pdf
```

**Multipart form** (field name `file`):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files?visibility=public" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@photo.jpg"
```

`201` response:
```json
{
  "id": "26d64a9b-c238-4446-8923-094ab3f090c8",
  "name": "report.pdf",
  "mime": "application/pdf",
  "size": 20481,
  "visibility": "private",
  "owner": "you@company.com",
  "createdAt": "2026-07-02T…Z",
  "url": "https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files/26d64a9b-…"
}
```

## Retrieve — `GET /api/v1/files/{id}`

Returns the raw bytes with the original `Content-Type` and filename.
- **Public** file → works with no auth (the `url` above is shareable).
- **Private** file → send `Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY` (owner/admin only), else `404`.

```bash
# public
curl https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files/$ID -o out.pdf
# private
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files/$ID -o out.pdf
```

Metadata only (JSON, no bytes): `GET /api/v1/files/{id}?meta=1`.

## Make public / private — `PATCH /api/v1/files/{id}`

```bash
curl -X PATCH https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files/$ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"visibility":"public"}'      # or "private"
```
Returns the updated metadata. Owner or admin only.

## List your files — `GET /api/v1/files`

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files
# → { "files": [ { id, name, mime, size, visibility, url, … }, … ] }
```

## Delete — `DELETE /api/v1/files/{id}`

```bash
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  https://gateway.getoffgridai.co/api/v1/files/$ID
# → { "deleted": true }
```

---

## Status codes
| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 201  | Uploaded |
| 200  | OK (retrieve / patch / list / delete) |
| 400  | Empty body / missing `file` field |
| 401  | Missing/invalid credentials on a write/list call |
| 404  | Not found, or a private file without access |

## Notes / limits
- Storage: server local disk (`OFFGRID_FILES_DIR`) + Postgres metadata. Fully on-prem.
- Auth is the **one key flow** used across Off Grid: Keycloak service-account JWTs,
  validated through a single `IdentityVerifier` seam (`src/lib/auth/token-verifier.ts`)
  shared by the Files API, the admin API, and the gateway. Add a new IdP by implementing
  that interface — no endpoint changes.
- `OFFGRID_ADMIN_TOKEN` still works as an explicit **break-glass** static token if set
  (bootstrap/CI), but the canonical path is a Keycloak-issued key.
- Served through the **network gateway** (`gateway.getoffgridai.co`), so file requests
  get the edge WAF + rate limit. The console host (`onprem-console.getoffgridai.co`)
  also serves the same API directly if you prefer.

name: CI

# The same gate the pre-push hook enforces locally, now enforced in CI on every push + PR:
# typecheck, tests, coverage >= 80% on all of statements/branches/functions/lines/conditions
# (c8 --check-coverage, thresholds in .c8rc.json), and a clean production build.
# A push/PR that drops below the bar fails here, not just on a developer's machine.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout console
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: console

      # The @offgrid/* packages are vendored in-repo under console/packages/ (with prebuilt
      # dist), so `npm ci` resolves the file: deps locally — no private-repo checkout needed.
      - name: Setup Node 22
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: console/package-lock.json

      - name: Install console deps
        working-directory: console
        run: npm ci

      - name: Verify pinned shared UI artifacts
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run verify:vendor

      - name: Typecheck
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Tests + coverage gate (>=80% all dimensions, enforced)
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run coverage:check

      # Static architecture gate: fails on any ERROR-level dependency-cruiser
      # violation — above all an eager-value circular import (the Node-22-only
      # TDZ prod-build crash class). WARN findings (type-only cycles, orphans)
      # are advisory and do not fail the job. Ruleset: .dependency-cruiser.js.
      - name: Dependency-cruiser gate (no circular imports / boundary breaks)
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run depcruise

      # DRY gate: fails only when code duplication exceeds the ratcheting
      # threshold in .jscpd.json — mechanically enforcing CLAUDE.md hygiene §C
      # ("duplicated logic that drifts is a defect"). Baseline-then-ratchet:
      # the threshold sits just above the real baseline and is ratcheted DOWN
      # as G-CPD-* clones are extracted (see docs/GAPS_BACKLOG.md).
      - name: jscpd DRY gate (code duplication under threshold)
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run jscpd

      - name: Production build
        working-directory: console
        run: npm run build

# One-IP edge proxy. Fronts the Console (UI + /api) and the Gateway (OpenAI-compatible /v1)
# behind a single address, so everyone on the office WiFi uses one URL.
# Brought up by ./setup.sh, which generates the Caddyfile next to this file.
services:
  edge:
    image: caddy:2.8-alpine
    container_name: offgrid-edge
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "${OFFGRID_PUBLIC_PORT:-80}:${OFFGRID_PUBLIC_PORT:-80}"
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
    extra_hosts:
      # lets the container reach a Console running with `next start` on the host
      - "host.docker.internal:host-gateway"

# Off Grid Console — THE canonical OSS stack. One file, all five planes, profiled by capability.
# Variants (lean / enterprise / air-gapped) are derived from this — never hand-rolled separately.
#
#   docker compose --profile all up -d              # full 5-layer depth (everything below)
#   docker compose --profile data --profile ai up   # pick planes/capabilities à la carte
#
# Profiles map 1:1 to capabilities, so a deployment runs only what it licensed:
#   data · secrets · observability · guardrails · policy · identity · lineage · llmops · agents · ai
#
# The Off Grid AI Gateway is first-party and runs SEPARATELY (127.0.0.1:7878) — never in compose.
# FinOps/cost + token issuance + per-user/per-project usage are FIRST-PARTY console capabilities
# (we own the gateway), not containers. All images here are permissive (Apache-2.0 / MIT / MPL-2.0
# / BSD / PostgreSQL) — see ../LICENSES.md. Dev-mode creds below are NOT for production.
name: offgrid-console

# Shared Airbyte env matrix — matched to airbytehq/airbyte-platform v0.63.15 .env + docker-compose.
# Top-level x- extension so it's a valid anchor source (Compose rejects bare keys under `services:`).
# Anchored so server/worker/bootloader stay in lockstep. SECRET_PERSISTENCE + CONFIG_DATABASE_* +
# INTERNAL_API_HOST are the version-specific requirements the old hand-rolled set was missing
# (worker died: "requires a bean ConnectionFactory with qualifier @Named('local-secrets')").
x-airbyte-env: &airbyte-env
  DATABASE_USER: airbyte
  DATABASE_PASSWORD: airbyte
  DATABASE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://airbyte-db:5432/airbyte
  DATABASE_HOST: airbyte-db
  DATABASE_PORT: '5432'
  DATABASE_DB: airbyte
  # ONE DB for jobs + configs here; CONFIG_DATABASE_* mirror DATABASE_* (server/bootloader define
  # `config` + `jobs` jOOQ datasources from these).
  # SECRET_PERSISTENCE is DELIBERATELY NOT in this shared anchor — it is set per-service (server +
  # worker only) to TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE, which registers the `local-secrets` jOOQ datasource
  # (built from DATABASE_*) that those two binaries require. The BOOTLOADER must NOT get it: with
  # TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE the bootloader crashes (NoSuchBeanException DSLContext @Named('local-
  # secrets')), so it stays on the NO_OP default. This split mirrors airbyte's official compose.
  CONFIG_DATABASE_USER: airbyte
  CONFIG_DATABASE_PASSWORD: airbyte
  CONFIG_DATABASE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://airbyte-db:5432/airbyte
  # NOTE on the `local-secrets` datasource: LocalTestingSecretPersistence (SECRET_PERSISTENCE=
  # TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE) needs a Micronaut Hikari datasource named `local-secrets`. It CANNOT be
  # supplied via env vars — Micronaut maps DATASOURCES_LOCAL_SECRETS_URL to `datasources.local.secrets.url`
  # (underscore→dot), producing a broken datasource named `local` ("No URL specified"). The hyphen in
  # `local-secrets` only survives as a JVM system property, so it's passed via JAVA_OPTS on the
  # server + worker services below (NOT here — the bootloader stays on NO_OP and must not build it).
  TEMPORAL_HOST: airbyte-temporal:7233
  INTERNAL_API_HOST: http://airbyte-server:8001
  WORKLOAD_API_HOST: http://airbyte-server:8001
  CONNECTOR_BUILDER_SERVER_API_HOST: http://airbyte-connector-builder-server:80
  WEBAPP_URL: http://localhost:8006/
  AIRBYTE_VERSION: 0.63.15
  DEPLOYMENT_MODE: OSS
  WORKSPACE_ROOT: /tmp/workspace
  WORKSPACE_DOCKER_MOUNT: airbyteworkspace
  LOCAL_ROOT: /tmp/airbyte_local
  LOCAL_DOCKER_MOUNT: /tmp/airbyte_local
  CONFIG_ROOT: /data
  TRACKING_STRATEGY: logging
  JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_REQUEST: ''
  JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_CPU_LIMIT: ''
  JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_REQUEST: ''
  JOB_MAIN_CONTAINER_MEMORY_LIMIT: ''
  WORKER_ENVIRONMENT: docker
  LOG_LEVEL: INFO
  # Micronaut bean profile. The worker registers its activity/spec workers only under the
  # `control-plane` environment; without it registerGetSpec() throws NoSuchElementException at boot.
  MICRONAUT_ENVIRONMENTS: control-plane
  # 0.63.x unified storage layer — worker/server resolve ${STORAGE_TYPE} + ${STORAGE_BUCKET_*} at
  # boot (worker crashed: "Could not resolve placeholder ${STORAGE_TYPE}"). LOCAL keeps logs/state on
  # the mounted workspace volume (no S3 needed for this dev-parity set); bucket names are still
  # required as keys even for LOCAL.
  STORAGE_TYPE: LOCAL
  STORAGE_BUCKET_LOG: airbyte-storage
  STORAGE_BUCKET_STATE: airbyte-storage
  STORAGE_BUCKET_WORKLOAD_OUTPUT: airbyte-storage
  STORAGE_BUCKET_ACTIVITY_PAYLOAD: airbyte-storage
  # Flyway baseline versions the server's application.yml resolves at boot (server crashed:
  # "property ${airbyte.flyway.configs.minimum-migration-version} doesn't exist"). Values per
  # airbyte's official 0.63.x .env.
  CONFIGS_DATABASE_MINIMUM_FLYWAY_MIGRATION_VERSION: 0.40.23.002
  JOBS_DATABASE_MINIMUM_FLYWAY_MIGRATION_VERSION: 0.40.26.001

services:
  # ── DATA PLANE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Postgres + pgvector: console state, append-only audit, AND the server-scale Brain vector store.
  postgres:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:0.8.0-pg16
    profiles: [data, ai, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: offgrid
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: offgrid
      POSTGRES_DB: offgrid_console
    ports: ['5432:5432']
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U offgrid']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

  # Object store for documents/artifacts (S3-compatible, Apache-2.0).
  seaweedfs:
    image: chrislusf/seaweedfs:3.80
    profiles: [data, all]
    command: 'server -dir=/data -s3 -s3.port=8333'
    ports: ['8333:8333', '9333:9333']
    volumes: [seaweed:/data]

  # ── AI PLANE — vector store alternative (Brain bridge) ─────────────────────────
  qdrant:
    image: qdrant/qdrant:v1.12.5
    profiles: [ai, all]
    ports: ['6333:6333']
    volumes: [qdrant:/qdrant/storage]

  # ── SECRETS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # DEV/local convenience: in-memory, auto-unsealed, hardcoded root token. Use for `make secrets`
  # locally ONLY — secrets do NOT survive a restart. Profile `secrets-dev`.
  openbao-dev:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.1.0
    profiles: [secrets-dev]
    cap_add: [IPC_LOCK]
    environment:
      BAO_DEV_ROOT_TOKEN_ID: offgrid-dev-token
      BAO_DEV_LISTEN_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8200
    ports: ['8200:8200']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'bao', 'status', '-address=http://127.0.0.1:8200']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

  # PROD: PERSISTENT file storage — secrets survive restarts (fixes the audit P0). Comes up SEALED;
  # first boot needs `bao operator init` + unseal (SUPERVISED — see SERVER_STATE.md § OpenBao
  # persistence migration). Back up the openbao-data volume. Now the default `secrets`/`all` profile.
  openbao:
    image: openbao/openbao:2.1.0
    profiles: [secrets, all]
    cap_add: [IPC_LOCK]
    command: ['server', '-config=/openbao/config/config.hcl']
    environment:
      BAO_ADDR: http://127.0.0.1:8200
    volumes:
      - ./openbao/config.hcl:/openbao/config/config.hcl:ro
      - openbao-data:/openbao/data
    ports: ['8200:8200']
    healthcheck:
      # `initialized=true` once set up; sealed status is fine for the healthcheck (server is up).
      test: ['CMD', 'bao', 'status', '-address=http://127.0.0.1:8200']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

  # ── IDENTITY (SSO) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Keycloak dev mode (in-memory H2) — self-contained for local; back with Postgres in prod.
  keycloak:
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.0.7
    profiles: [identity, all]
    # --import-realm re-imports keycloak/offgrid-realm.json on every boot, so the realm + client +
    # test user are deterministic and survive `make down` — no runtime setup script needed. (Dev
    # mode; for production use a real DB + secrets and remove the committed dev secret.)
    command: ['start-dev', '--import-realm']
    environment:
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_USERNAME: admin
      KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD: offgrid-dev
      KC_HTTP_PORT: '8080'
    volumes:
      - ./keycloak:/opt/keycloak/data/import:ro
    ports: ['8080:8080']

  # ── POLICY (policy-as-code) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  opa:
    image: openpolicyagent/opa:0.70.0
    profiles: [policy, all]
    command: ['run', '--server', '--addr=0.0.0.0:8181', '--log-level=error']
    # Stock OPA has ZERO auth — bind to loopback so only same-host next-server reaches it.
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:8181:8181']

  # ── GUARDRAILS (PII detection / redaction) ────────────────────────────────────────
  # Stock Presidio images have ZERO auth — bind to loopback so only same-host next-server
  # (OFFGRID_PRESIDIO_URL / _ANONYMIZER_URL) reaches them, never the LAN.
  presidio-analyzer:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-analyzer:2.2.356
    profiles: [guardrails, all]
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:5002:3000']
  presidio-anonymizer:
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/presidio-anonymizer:2.2.356
    profiles: [guardrails, all]
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:5001:3000']

  # Actual Microsoft Presidio image-redactor library, kept separate from the stock text services.
  # Raw pixels are processed in memory with Tesseract scratch space on tmpfs; no image volume exists.
  presidio-image-redactor:
    image: offgrid/presidio-image-redactor:0.0.59-ogac.1
    build:
      context: ./sidecars/presidio-image-redactor
    profiles: [guardrails, all]
    environment:
      PRESIDIO_IMAGE_REDACTOR_TOKEN: ${PRESIDIO_IMAGE_REDACTOR_TOKEN:-change-me}
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:5003:8004']
    read_only: true
    tmpfs: ['/tmp:size=64m,mode=1777']
    security_opt: ['no-new-privileges:true']
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    mem_limit: 2g
    cpus: 2
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          'CMD-SHELL',
          'python -c "import os,urllib.request; r=urllib.request.Request(''http://127.0.0.1:8004/health'',headers={''Authorization'':''Bearer ''+os.environ[''PRESIDIO_IMAGE_REDACTOR_TOKEN'']}); urllib.request.urlopen(r,timeout=20).read()"',
        ]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 25s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 120s

  # LLM Guard (Protect AI, MIT) — a NAMED alternative guardrails engine (scanner suite: Anonymize,
  # Secrets, Sensitive, Toxicity, Bias, BanTopics, PromptInjection, Language, Regex, TokenLimit).
  # Selected with OFFGRID_ADAPTER_GUARDRAILS=llm-guard; the console reaches it at
  # OFFGRID_HTTP_GUARDRAIL_URL (POST /analyze/prompt) with the AUTH_TOKEN as _API_KEY.
  #
  # Image note: the canonical DOCUMENTED image is `laiyer/llm-guard-api` (Laiyer → Protect AI; the
  # deploy docs were never re-tagged to a protectai image, and no ghcr image is published). Pinned to
  # 0.3.16, the latest published tag (pushed 2025-05-19). Heads-up: the upstream repo is ARCHIVED
  # (EOL) as of mid-2026 — it still runs, but factor that into any long-term dependency. Use the
  # `-cuda` variant for GPU. Health: GET /healthz (liveness) / /readyz (readiness). Loopback-bound so
  # only the same-host next-server reaches it — set AUTH_TOKEN in .env before exposing it anywhere.
  llm-guard:
    image: laiyer/llm-guard-api:0.3.16
    profiles: [guardrails, all]
    environment:
      - LOG_LEVEL=INFO
      - AUTH_TOKEN=${LLM_GUARD_AUTH_TOKEN:-change-me}
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:8000:8000']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'curl', '-fsS', 'http://localhost:8000/healthz']
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ── OBSERVABILITY (metrics/logs/traces — one OTLP wire, any backend) ───────────────
  victoriametrics:
    image: victoriametrics/victoria-metrics:v1.106.1
    profiles: [observability, all]
    command: ['-storageDataPath=/vmdata', '-httpListenAddr=:8428', '-retentionPeriod=1']
    ports: ['8428:8428']
    volumes: [vmdata:/vmdata]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'wget', '-qO-', 'http://127.0.0.1:8428/health']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12
  victorialogs:
    image: victoriametrics/victoria-logs:v1.3.2-victorialogs
    profiles: [observability, all]
    command: ['-storageDataPath=/vldata', '-httpListenAddr=:9428']
    ports: ['9428:9428']
    volumes: [vldata:/vldata]
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.116.0
    profiles: [observability, all]
    command: ['--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml']
    volumes: ['./otel-collector.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro']
    ports: ['4318:4318', '4317:4317']
    depends_on: [victoriametrics, jaeger]

  # LiteLLM Proxy — the model-door ROUTER. OpenAI-compatible, so it drops in behind the console's
  # GATEWAY_URL (set OFFGRID_GATEWAY_URL=http://litellm:4000 to cut over) and replaces the hand-rolled
  # aggregator with health-checked load-balancing, automatic failover/retries, per-key budgets + rate
  # limits, and structured request logging. It routes across the on-prem fleet nodes (192.168.1.x:7878)
  # AND the configured cloud providers. The mounted config.yaml is generated from the console's own
  # view of the fleet — see src/lib/litellm-config.ts (deploy/litellm-config.yaml is the committed
  # sample; regenerate it from the live pool). The aggregator (scripts/cluster-gateway.mjs) stays
  # available as a fallback until this is verified live.
  litellm:
    image: ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable
    profiles: [ai, all]
    command: ['--config', '/app/config.yaml', '--port', '4000', '--num_workers', '4']
    ports: ['4000:4000']
    volumes: ['./litellm-config.yaml:/app/config.yaml:ro']
    environment:
      # Master key gate for the management APIs (/model|/key|/health) the console Router view reads.
      OFFGRID_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY: ${OFFGRID_LITELLM_MASTER_KEY:-sk-litellm-dev-change-me}
      # Cloud provider keys resolved at runtime via os.environ/… refs in config.yaml (never committed).
      OFFGRID_CLOUD_OPENAI_API_KEY: ${OFFGRID_CLOUD_OPENAI_API_KEY:-}
      OFFGRID_CLOUD_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${OFFGRID_CLOUD_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:-}
      OFFGRID_CLOUD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ${OFFGRID_CLOUD_DEEPSEEK_API_KEY:-}
      OFFGRID_CLOUD_ZHIPU_API_KEY: ${OFFGRID_CLOUD_ZHIPU_API_KEY:-}
      OFFGRID_CLOUD_COMPAT_API_KEY: ${OFFGRID_CLOUD_COMPAT_API_KEY:-}
      # Structured request logging → the same offgrid-gateway OpenSearch index the traffic/logs UI
      # reads (litellm-log-shape.ts maps the callback payload into the TrafficRecord shape).
      OFFGRID_OPENSEARCH_URL: ${OFFGRID_OPENSEARCH_URL:-http://opensearch:9200}
      OFFGRID_GATEWAY_INDEX: ${OFFGRID_GATEWAY_INDEX:-offgrid-gateway}
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'curl', '-f', 'http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness']
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  # Distributed-trace backend (app-layer tracing): OTLP in → queryable trace UI on :16686.
  jaeger:
    image: jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.62.0
    profiles: [observability, all]
    environment:
      COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED: 'true'
    ports: ['16686:16686']

  # ── LLMOps (LLM tracing, evals, cost per trace/user/project) ──────────────────────
  langfuse-db:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: langfuse
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: langfuse
      POSTGRES_DB: langfuse
    volumes: [langfusedb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U langfuse']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  # Langfuse v3 — split web + worker, backed by ClickHouse (analytics), MinIO (event blobs) and
  # Redis (queue), in addition to the Postgres above. v3 is what accepts OTLP traces directly
  # (POST /api/public/otel/v1/traces), so the console's span fan-out lands here. Heavier than v2
  # (4 extra containers) → scoped to the llmops/all profiles; `make smoke`/`down` are unaffected.
  langfuse-clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8-alpine
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_USER: clickhouse
      CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: clickhouse
    ulimits:
      nofile: { soft: 262144, hard: 262144 }
    volumes:
      - clickhouse:/var/lib/clickhouse
      - clickhouselogs:/var/log/clickhouse-server
    healthcheck:
      test:
        ['CMD-SHELL', 'wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://127.0.0.1:8123/ping || exit 1']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  langfuse-minio:
    image: minio/minio:RELEASE.2024-11-07T00-52-20Z
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    entrypoint: sh
    # pre-create the event bucket so Langfuse's S3 client finds it on first write
    command: -c 'mkdir -p /data/langfuse && minio server --address ":9000" --console-address ":9001" /data'
    environment:
      MINIO_ROOT_USER: minio
      MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD: miniosecret
    volumes: [langfuseminio:/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'mc', 'ready', 'local']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  langfuse-redis:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    command: ['redis-server', '--maxmemory-policy', 'noeviction']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  langfuse-worker:
    image: langfuse/langfuse-worker:3.30.0
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      langfuse-db: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-clickhouse: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-minio: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment: &langfuse-env
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://langfuse:langfuse@langfuse-db:5432/langfuse
      SALT: offgrid-dev-salt
      ENCRYPTION_KEY: 1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef
      TELEMETRY_ENABLED: 'false'
      CLICKHOUSE_MIGRATION_URL: clickhouse://langfuse-clickhouse:9000
      CLICKHOUSE_URL: http://langfuse-clickhouse:8123
      CLICKHOUSE_USER: clickhouse
      CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: clickhouse
      CLICKHOUSE_CLUSTER_ENABLED: 'false'
      REDIS_HOST: langfuse-redis
      REDIS_PORT: '6379'
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_BUCKET: langfuse
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_REGION: auto
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_ACCESS_KEY_ID: minio
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: miniosecret
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_ENDPOINT: http://langfuse-minio:9000
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_FORCE_PATH_STYLE: 'true'
      LANGFUSE_S3_EVENT_UPLOAD_PREFIX: events/
  langfuse:
    image: langfuse/langfuse:3.30.0
    profiles: [llmops, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      langfuse-worker: { condition: service_started }
      langfuse-db: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-clickhouse: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-minio: { condition: service_healthy }
      langfuse-redis: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      <<: *langfuse-env
      NEXTAUTH_URL: http://localhost:3030
      NEXTAUTH_SECRET: offgrid-dev-secret
      # Headless bootstrap: create an org/project + a fixed API key pair on first boot, so the
      # OTLP auth header is known ahead of time (no manual click-through to get keys).
      LANGFUSE_INIT_ORG_ID: offgrid
      LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_ID: console
      LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_PUBLIC_KEY: pk-lf-offgrid-console
      LANGFUSE_INIT_PROJECT_SECRET_KEY: sk-lf-offgrid-console
      LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_EMAIL: dev@offgrid.local
      LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_PASSWORD: offgrid-dev-pw
      LANGFUSE_INIT_USER_NAME: Off Grid Dev
    ports: ['3030:3000']

  # ── LINEAGE & PROVENANCE (source → chunk → answer) ────────────────────────────────
  marquez-db:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [lineage, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: marquez
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: marquez
      POSTGRES_DB: marquez
    volumes: [marquezdb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U marquez']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  marquez:
    image: marquezproject/marquez:0.50.0
    profiles: [lineage, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      marquez-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      MARQUEZ_PORT: '5000'
      MARQUEZ_ADMIN_PORT: '5010'
      POSTGRES_HOST: marquez-db
      POSTGRES_PORT: '5432'
      POSTGRES_DB: marquez
      POSTGRES_USER: marquez
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: marquez
    # Stock Marquez has ZERO auth — bind to loopback so only same-host next-server reads it.
    # marquez-web reaches marquez over the internal Docker network (MARQUEZ_HOST), unaffected.
    ports: ['127.0.0.1:9000:5000', '127.0.0.1:5010:5010']
  marquez-web:
    image: marquezproject/marquez-web:0.50.0
    profiles: [lineage, all]
    depends_on: [marquez]
    environment:
      MARQUEZ_HOST: marquez
      MARQUEZ_PORT: '5000'
      WEB_PORT: '3000'
    ports: ['3001:3000']

  # ── AGENT RUNTIME (durable workflows) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  temporal-db:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [agents, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: temporal
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: temporal
      POSTGRES_DB: temporal
    volumes: [temporaldb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U temporal']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  temporal:
    image: temporalio/auto-setup:1.25.2
    profiles: [agents, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      temporal-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DB: postgres12
      DB_PORT: '5432'
      POSTGRES_USER: temporal
      POSTGRES_PWD: temporal
      POSTGRES_SEEDS: temporal-db
    ports: ['7233:7233']
  temporal-ui:
    image: temporalio/ui:2.32.0
    profiles: [agents, all]
    depends_on: [temporal]
    environment:
      TEMPORAL_ADDRESS: temporal:7233
    ports: ['8081:8080']

  # ── CACHING & RATE LIMITS (Redis: semantic/exact response cache + rate limiting) ──
  redis:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    profiles: [caching, all]
    command: ['redis-server', '--save', '', '--appendonly', 'no']
    ports: ['6379:6379']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'redis-cli', 'ping']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 12

  # ── SIEM (OpenSearch: audit/log search + dashboards) ──────────────────────────────
  opensearch:
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch:2.18.0
    profiles: [siem, all]
    environment:
      discovery.type: single-node
      DISABLE_SECURITY_PLUGIN: 'true'
      OPENSEARCH_JAVA_OPTS: '-Xms512m -Xmx512m'
      bootstrap.memory_lock: 'true'
    ulimits:
      memlock: { soft: -1, hard: -1 }
    ports: ['9200:9200']
    volumes: [opensearch:/usr/share/opensearch/data]
  opensearch-dashboards:
    image: opensearchproject/opensearch-dashboards:2.18.0
    profiles: [siem, all]
    depends_on: [opensearch]
    environment:
      OPENSEARCH_HOSTS: '["http://opensearch:9200"]'
      DISABLE_SECURITY_DASHBOARDS_PLUGIN: 'true'
    ports: ['5601:5601']

  # ── FEATURE FLAGS (Unleash: modular capability/module control) ────────────────────
  unleash-db:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [flags, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: unleash
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: unleash
      POSTGRES_DB: unleash
    volumes: [unleashdb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U unleash']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  unleash:
    image: unleashorg/unleash-server:6.6
    profiles: [flags, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      unleash-db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://unleash:unleash@unleash-db:5432/unleash
      DATABASE_SSL: 'false'
    ports: ['4242:4242']

  # ── AGENT QA SIDECARS (Apache-2.0 Python wrappers for the eval/drift swap-ins) ────────
  # Thin services the console's `ragas` (evals) and `evidently` (drift) adapters call. Both run
  # their metrics through the on-device gateway; kept as sidecars so the console stays Node-only.
  evidently:
    build: ./sidecars/drift
    profiles: [qa, all]
    ports: ['8001:8001']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'python -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://127.0.0.1:8001/\")"']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
  ragas:
    build: ./sidecars/ragas
    profiles: [qa, all]
    ports: ['8002:8002']
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'python -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://127.0.0.1:8002/health\")"']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  # ── BI / DATA EXPLORATION (Apache Superset: view, SQL, pivot/transpose, dashboards) ──
  # First run: `docker compose exec superset superset init` (creates admin + metadata).
  superset:
    image: apache/superset:4.1.1
    profiles: [bi, all]
    environment:
      SUPERSET_SECRET_KEY: offgrid-dev-superset-secret
    ports: ['8088:8088']
    volumes: [superset:/app/superset_home]

  # ── MDM / FLEET CONTROL (FleetDM: osquery-based cross-platform device management) ──────
  # MIT-licensed Fleet Free. First run, create an admin + API token:
  #   docker compose exec fleet fleetctl setup --email a@b.co --password '...' --org-name OffGrid
  #   then `fleetctl login` + `fleetctl get api-token` → set OFFGRID_FLEET_TOKEN.
  fleet-mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0.40
    profiles: [mdm, all]
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: fleet
      MYSQL_DATABASE: fleet
      MYSQL_USER: fleet
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: fleet
    volumes: [fleetmysql:/var/lib/mysql]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'mysqladmin', 'ping', '-h', '127.0.0.1', '-ufleet', '-pfleet']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30
  fleet-redis:
    image: redis:7.4-alpine
    profiles: [mdm, all]
  fleet:
    image: fleetdm/fleet:v4.87.0
    profiles: [mdm, all]
    depends_on:
      fleet-mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
    command: sh -c "fleet prepare db --no-prompt && fleet serve"
    environment:
      FLEET_MYSQL_ADDRESS: fleet-mysql:3306
      FLEET_MYSQL_DATABASE: fleet
      FLEET_MYSQL_USERNAME: fleet
      FLEET_MYSQL_PASSWORD: fleet
      FLEET_REDIS_ADDRESS: fleet-redis:6379
      FLEET_SERVER_ADDRESS: 0.0.0.0:8070
      FLEET_SERVER_TLS: 'false'
      FLEET_LOGGING_JSON: 'true'
    ports: ['8070:8070']

  # ══ DATA PLANE (NEW — S2-only) ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # The second substrate engine (the first is the model engine — the llama.cpp gateway fleet).
  # This is the DATA engine: warehouse + streaming + connectors/CDC + data-quality. It is heavy
  # (Airbyte alone is ~8 containers) and is intended to run on offgrid-s2 (16GB M1) under Colima,
  # NOT on S1 alongside the control plane. See onprem/DATA_PLANE.md for the S2 bringup runbook.
  # All images below are permissive-licensed (Apache-2.0 / MIT / ELv2* / BSD) — dev creds are NOT
  # for production. (*Redpanda core is BSL/permissive-for-single-node dev use; swap for a licensed
  # broker or Apache Kafka in production if that matters to you.)

  # ── WAREHOUSE (ClickHouse — columnar analytics store; what BI/PowerBI reads) ────────
  # STANDALONE and DISTINCT from the langfuse-clickhouse above (that one is llmops-internal).
  # Own service name, own volume, own ports (8124/9001) so the two never collide.
  warehouse-clickhouse:
    image: clickhouse/clickhouse-server:24.8-alpine
    profiles: [warehouse, all]
    environment:
      CLICKHOUSE_USER: warehouse
      CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD: warehouse # DEV ONLY — not for production
      CLICKHOUSE_DB: offgrid_warehouse
    ulimits:
      nofile: { soft: 262144, hard: 262144 }
    # HTTP 8124 (native SQL over HTTP; what dbt / BI point at) + native TCP 9001. Ports are shifted
    # off ClickHouse defaults (8123/9000) so they don't clash with langfuse-clickhouse or Marquez.
    ports: ['8124:8123', '9001:9000']
    volumes:
      - warehouseclickhouse:/var/lib/clickhouse
      - warehouseclickhouselogs:/var/log/clickhouse-server
    healthcheck:
      test:
        ['CMD-SHELL', 'wget --no-verbose --tries=1 --spider http://127.0.0.1:8123/ping || exit 1']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20

  # ── STREAMING / MQ (Redpanda — Kafka-API broker, single container, lighter than Kafka) ──
  redpanda:
    image: redpandadata/redpanda:v24.2.7
    profiles: [streaming, all]
    command:
      - redpanda
      - start
      - --smp=1 # 1 core — keep S2 footprint small
      - --memory=1G # bounded so it co-exists with Airbyte + ClickHouse on 16GB
      - --reserve-memory=0M
      - --overprovisioned
      - --node-id=0
      - --check=false
      # Kafka API on 9092 (internal) + 19092 (host); admin 9644; Schema Registry 8081.
      - --kafka-addr=internal://0.0.0.0:9092,external://0.0.0.0:19092
      - --advertise-kafka-addr=internal://redpanda:9092,external://127.0.0.1:19092
      - --schema-registry-addr=0.0.0.0:8081
    ports:
      - '19092:19092' # Kafka API (external)
      - '9644:9644' # admin API / metrics
      - '18083:8081' # schema registry
    volumes: [redpanda:/var/lib/redpanda/data]
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          'CMD-SHELL',
          'rpk cluster health | grep -q "Healthy:.*true" && curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8081/subjects >/dev/null',
        ]
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20

  # ── CONNECTORS + CDC (Airbyte OSS — the ELT engine, 300+ connectors + Debezium CDC) ──
  # HONEST: Airbyte is inherently multi-container. This is the minimal viable OSS set — its own
  # Postgres + Temporal + server + worker + webapp + connector-builder (~8 containers incl. deps).
  # It is HEAVY (~4–6GB RAM working set) and S2-ONLY. In production the vendor-recommended install
  # is `abctl` (a k3d/kind cluster); this compose set is the lean dev-parity path. Landing/lake zone
  # for extracted data is the EXISTING SeaweedFS S3 (see note below) — no separate object store here.
  airbyte-db:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [etl, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: airbyte
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: airbyte # DEV ONLY — not for production
      POSTGRES_DB: airbyte
    volumes: [airbytedb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U airbyte']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
  # Bootloader runs the Flyway DB migrations + connector-catalog seed, then exits. Server/worker
  # MUST wait for it (service_completed_successfully) — without it the schema is absent and they die.
  airbyte-bootloader:
    image: airbyte/bootloader:0.63.15
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-db: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      <<: *airbyte-env

  # Airbyte runs its own Temporal (workflow engine for sync jobs) — SEPARATE from the agents-profile
  # `temporal` above (different DB, different network role). Airbyte auto-creates its schema.
  # v0.63.15 requires the dynamicconfig file mounted at config/dynamicconfig/development.yaml — the
  # old `development-sql.yaml` path does not exist in this image (crash: "no such file or directory").
  airbyte-temporal:
    image: temporalio/auto-setup:1.23.1
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-db: { condition: service_healthy }
    environment:
      DB: postgresql
      DB_PORT: '5432'
      POSTGRES_USER: airbyte
      POSTGRES_PWD: airbyte
      POSTGRES_SEEDS: airbyte-db
      DYNAMIC_CONFIG_FILE_PATH: config/dynamicconfig/development.yaml
    volumes:
      - ./airbyte/temporal/dynamicconfig:/etc/temporal/config/dynamicconfig
  airbyte-server:
    image: airbyte/server:0.63.15
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-db: { condition: service_healthy }
      airbyte-bootloader: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      airbyte-temporal: { condition: service_started }
    environment:
      <<: *airbyte-env
      SECRET_PERSISTENCE: TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE
      # Defines the hyphenated `local-secrets` Hikari datasource that TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE needs
      # (env vars can't express the hyphen — see the anchor note). Points at the same airbyte DB.
      # Use JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (JVM APPENDS it) NOT JAVA_OPTS — JAVA_OPTS would REPLACE the image's
      # baked JVM opts and break the server's Flyway property resolution at boot.
      JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS: >-
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.url=jdbc:postgresql://airbyte-db:5432/airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.username=airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.password=airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.driver-class-name=org.postgresql.Driver
    ports: ['8005:8001'] # internal API (webapp proxies to it)
    volumes:
      - airbyteworkspace:/tmp/workspace
      - airbytedata:/data
  airbyte-worker:
    image: airbyte/worker:0.63.15
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-bootloader: { condition: service_completed_successfully }
      airbyte-server: { condition: service_started }
      airbyte-temporal: { condition: service_started }
    environment:
      # The worker launches connector containers, so it needs the host Docker socket (S2 OrbStack).
      <<: *airbyte-env
      SECRET_PERSISTENCE: TESTING_CONFIG_DB_TABLE
      # Defines the hyphenated `local-secrets` Hikari datasource (see server + anchor notes).
      # JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS (appended by the JVM) — never JAVA_OPTS, which replaces the image defaults.
      JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS: >-
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.url=jdbc:postgresql://airbyte-db:5432/airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.username=airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.password=airbyte
        -Ddatasources.local-secrets.driver-class-name=org.postgresql.Driver
    volumes:
      - airbyteworkspace:/tmp/workspace
      - airbytedata:/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
  airbyte-webapp:
    image: airbyte/webapp:0.63.15
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-server: { condition: service_started }
    environment:
      # v0.63.15 nginx template interpolates AIRBYTE_SERVER_HOST + CONNECTOR_BUILDER_API_HOST +
      # KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_HOST (NOT INTERNAL_API_HOST). Any missing ⇒ nginx "host not found in
      # upstream". Keycloak isn't deployed in this OSS set, so point it at localhost (the default in
      # airbyte's own compose) — the /auth upstream is simply never hit.
      AIRBYTE_SERVER_HOST: airbyte-server:8001
      CONNECTOR_BUILDER_API_HOST: airbyte-connector-builder-server:80
      KEYCLOAK_INTERNAL_HOST: localhost
    ports: ['8006:8080'] # 0.63.15 webapp nginx listens on 8080 (NOT 80). Airbyte UI → OFFGRID_AIRBYTE_URL=http://<s2>:8006
  airbyte-connector-builder-server:
    image: airbyte/connector-builder-server:0.63.15
    profiles: [etl, all]
    restart: on-failure
    depends_on:
      airbyte-server: { condition: service_started }

  # ── DATA-LAKE LANDING ZONE ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # NOTE: no new object store here BY DESIGN. The lake landing/staging zone is the EXISTING
  # `seaweedfs` service (S3-compatible, :8333) under the `data` profile. Airbyte's S3 destination
  # points at it (bucket `offgrid-lake`, endpoint http://<s2-or-s1>:8333, path-style). Only add a
  # dedicated MinIO if a connector strictly needs an isolated bucket namespace — prefer SeaweedFS.

  # ── DATA QUALITY (Great Expectations sidecar — mirrors the evidently/ragas sidecar pattern) ──
  # GX Core 1.19 lifecycle service: authenticated tenant-scoped suite CRUD, governed asset
  # inspection, real GX validations, and retained validation results. State is a named volume; the
  # service token is supplied by the deployment environment and is never committed.
  great-expectations:
    build: ./sidecars/great-expectations
    profiles: [dataquality, all]
    # Safe generic default: loopback-only. The private fleet runbook may set
    # OFFGRID_DATA_PLANE_BIND to the node's private LAN address so the Console edge proxy can reach
    # it; never bind this unauthenticated legacy compatibility route to 0.0.0.0/public interfaces.
    ports: ['${OFFGRID_DATA_PLANE_BIND:-127.0.0.1}:8003:8003']
    environment:
      GX_STATE_ROOT: /var/lib/offgrid-gx
      OFFGRID_GX_SERVICE_TOKEN: ${OFFGRID_GX_SERVICE_TOKEN:-}
    volumes:
      - gxdata:/var/lib/offgrid-gx
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'python -c "import urllib.request;urllib.request.urlopen(\"http://127.0.0.1:8003/\")"']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  # ── ETL / orchestration engine (Kestra) — the visual pipeline + custom-code + trigger engine.
  # Governed behind the console's pipeline contract; surfaced in the Data tab in product language
  # ("Data movement / ETL orchestration" — never "Kestra" in the UI). Runs on S2 with the data plane.
  kestra-postgres:
    image: postgres:16.6-alpine
    profiles: [kestra, all]
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: kestra
      POSTGRES_USER: kestra
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: kestra
    volumes: [kestradb:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U kestra -d kestra']
      interval: 10s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
  kestra:
    image: kestra/kestra:latest  # TODO pin by digest once pulled with a manifest
    profiles: [kestra, all]
    restart: unless-stopped
    user: root
    command: server standalone
    depends_on:
      kestra-postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - kestradata:/app/storage
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock  # so Docker-task (custom code) nodes can run
      - /tmp/kestra-wd:/tmp/kestra-wd
    environment:
      # JVM capped so it co-exists with Airbyte/ClickHouse on the 16GB S2 box.
      JAVA_OPTS: '-Xmx1200m'
      KESTRA_CONFIGURATION: |
        datasources:
          postgres:
            url: jdbc:postgresql://kestra-postgres:5432/kestra
            driverClassName: org.postgresql.Driver
            username: kestra
            password: kestra
        kestra:
          server:
            # Kestra OSS 0.24+ REQUIRES basic auth (the `enabled` flag is ignored). Username must be a
            # valid email. These are DEMO credentials on the demo box (recorded in fleet SECRET_INVENTORY);
            # the console's Kestra adapter authenticates the API with them.
            basicAuth:
              username: admin@offgrid.local
              password: OffGridKestra2026
          repository:
            type: postgres
          storage:
            type: local
            local:
              basePath: /app/storage
          queue:
            type: postgres
          tasks:
            tmpDir:
              path: /tmp/kestra-wd
          url: http://localhost:8090/
    ports: ['8090:8080'] # Kestra UI/API :8080 → host 8090 (edge loopback 8945 → this)
    healthcheck:
      # The image has Bash but no curl/wget. Probe the in-container API listener so a running JVM
      # whose HTTP server failed to start cannot be reported healthy through Docker's host proxy.
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'bash -c "</dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/8080"']
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 60s

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Off Grid — office fleet bootstrap (MacBooks on a normal LAN)
#
# Run this on ONE Mac (the "core"). It asks for the OTHER Macs' IPs, reaches them
# over SSH, brings the stack up across the fleet, and hands you ONE URL.
#
# Topology it builds:
#   • THIS Mac (core)      → Postgres (docker) + Console (host) + Caddy edge (docker)
#   • Gateway Mac(s)       → Off Grid Desktop headless, run NATIVELY (Metal inference;
#                             cannot be containerized on macOS) — started over SSH.
#   • Everyone's browser   → http://<core-ip>:<public-port>   (one IP, via Caddy)
#
# Why not pure `docker compose up` across the fleet:
#   - macOS containers get no GPU/Metal, so the gateway must run native on its Mac.
#   - the Console currently runs as a host process (no Dockerfile yet).
#   Everything else is containerized and driven remotely via `docker context` + SSH.
#
# Re-runnable. Non-interactive: pre-set the CORE_IP / GATEWAY / SSH_USER / etc. env
# vars and answers are taken from them (used by CI / piped runs).
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
set -euo pipefail

DEPLOY_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
CONSOLE_DIR="$(cd "$DEPLOY_DIR/.." && pwd)"

c_b=$'\033[1m'; c_g=$'\033[32m'; c_y=$'\033[33m'; c_r=$'\033[31m'; c_0=$'\033[0m'
say()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
hd()   { printf '\n%s── %s ──%s\n' "$c_b" "$*" "$c_0"; }
ok()   { printf '%s✓%s %s\n' "$c_g" "$c_0" "$*"; }
warn() { printf '%s!%s %s\n' "$c_y" "$c_0" "$*"; }
die()  { printf '%s✗ %s%s\n' "$c_r" "$*" "$c_0" >&2; exit 1; }

ask() { # ask VAR "prompt" "default"  — honors a pre-set env var of the same name
  local __v=$1 __p=$2 __d=${3:-} __cur=${!1:-} __in
  if [ -n "$__cur" ]; then printf -v "$__v" '%s' "$__cur"; say "$__p ${c_g}$__cur${c_0} (from env)"; return; fi
  if [ -t 0 ]; then read -rp "$__p${__d:+ [$__d]}: " __in || true; else __in=""; fi
  printf -v "$__v" '%s' "${__in:-$__d}"
}

guess_ip() { ipconfig getifaddr en0 2>/dev/null || ipconfig getifaddr en1 2>/dev/null || hostname; }

hd "Off Grid office setup"
command -v docker >/dev/null || die "Docker not found. Install Docker Desktop on this Mac first."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker daemon not running. Start Docker Desktop."
command -v node   >/dev/null || die "Node not found (need >=20 for the Console)."

# ── 1. core identity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ask CORE_IP       "This Mac's LAN IP"                 "$(guess_ip)"
ask PUBLIC_PORT   "Public port for the one URL"       "80"
ask AUTH_MODE     "Auth (dev = open on LAN / keycloak)" "dev"

# ── 2. the OTHER Macs (gateways) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
hd "Gateway machine(s) — where inference runs (native Off Grid Desktop)"
say "Enter the IP of each gateway Mac. Blank line when done. Leave empty to run the"
say "gateway on THIS Mac (all-in-one)."
ask SSH_USER      "SSH username for the other Macs"   "$(whoami)"

GATEWAYS=()
if [ -n "${GATEWAY:-}" ]; then
  # non-interactive: GATEWAY may be a comma/space list
  IFS=', ' read -r -a GATEWAYS <<< "$GATEWAY"
elif [ -t 0 ]; then
  while true; do read -rp "  gateway Mac IP (enter to stop): " g || break; [ -z "$g" ] && break; GATEWAYS+=("$g"); done
fi
[ ${#GATEWAYS[@]} -eq 0 ] && { GATEWAYS=("$CORE_IP"); warn "No gateway IP given — using this Mac as the gateway too (all-in-one)."; }
GW_PRIMARY="${GATEWAYS[0]}"
GW_PORT="${GW_PORT:-7878}"

say ""
ok "Core (console/db/edge): $CORE_IP   public URL → http://$CORE_IP:$PUBLIC_PORT"
ok "Gateway(s):             ${GATEWAYS[*]}  (port $GW_PORT)"
ok "Auth mode:              $AUTH_MODE"

# ── 3. reach each gateway Mac over SSH, register a docker context ─────────────
hd "Checking the other Macs (SSH)"
SSH_OPTS="-o ConnectTimeout=6 -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new"
for gw in "${GATEWAYS[@]}"; do
  [ "$gw" = "$CORE_IP" ] && { ok "$gw is this Mac — local."; continue; }
  if ssh $SSH_OPTS "${SSH_USER}@${gw}" 'echo ok' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    ok "SSH to ${SSH_USER}@${gw} works."
    if ssh $SSH_OPTS "${SSH_USER}@${gw}" 'command -v docker >/dev/null && docker info >/dev/null 2>&1'; then
      ok "  Docker is up on $gw."
    else
      warn "  Docker not running on $gw — needed only if you containerize services there."
    fi
    # a docker context lets us drive `docker` on that Mac from here
    docker context rm "offgrid-$gw" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    docker context create "offgrid-$gw" --docker "host=ssh://${SSH_USER}@${gw}" >/dev/null
    ok "  docker context 'offgrid-$gw' registered."
  else
    warn "Cannot SSH to ${SSH_USER}@${gw}."
    warn "  On that Mac: System Settings → General → Sharing → enable 'Remote Login',"
    warn "  then from here run:  ssh-copy-id ${SSH_USER}@${gw}"
  fi
done

# ── 4. write Console env ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
hd "Writing Console config"
SECRET="${AUTH_SECRET:-$(openssl rand -base64 32)}"
{
  echo "DATABASE_URL=postgresql://offgrid@localhost:5432/offgrid_console"
  echo "AUTH_SECRET=$SECRET"
  echo "NODE_ENV=production"
  echo "OFFGRID_GATEWAY_URL=http://$GW_PRIMARY:$GW_PORT"
  [ "$AUTH_MODE" = "dev" ] && echo "AUTH_DEV_LOGIN=true"
} > "$CONSOLE_DIR/.env"
ok "Wrote $CONSOLE_DIR/.env  (gateway → http://$GW_PRIMARY:$GW_PORT)"

# ── 5. generate the one-IP Caddy edge config ─────────────────────────────────
cat > "$DEPLOY_DIR/Caddyfile" <<EOF
# Generated by setup.sh — one address fronts the whole stack.
:$PUBLIC_PORT {
	# OpenAI-compatible gateway API
	handle /v1/* {
		reverse_proxy $GW_PRIMARY:$GW_PORT
	}
	handle /healthz {
		reverse_proxy $GW_PRIMARY:$GW_PORT
	}
	# everything else → the Console (running on the host)
	handle {
		reverse_proxy host.docker.internal:3000
	}
}
EOF
ok "Wrote $DEPLOY_DIR/Caddyfile"

# ── 6. bring up the stack ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
hd "Bringing up Postgres (docker, this Mac)"
( cd "$DEPLOY_DIR" && docker compose --profile data up -d postgres )
ok "Postgres up on :5432"

hd "Console (host process)"
( cd "$CONSOLE_DIR"
  [ -d node_modules ] || npm ci
  npm run db:push
  npm run build
  # kill any prior instance, then start detached, bound to all interfaces
  pkill -f "next start -H 0.0.0.0 -p 3000" 2>/dev/null || true
  nohup npx next start -H 0.0.0.0 -p 3000 > "$DEPLOY_DIR/console.log" 2>&1 &
)
ok "Console starting on :3000 (logs: $DEPLOY_DIR/console.log)"

hd "Edge proxy (docker) — the one IP"
( cd "$DEPLOY_DIR" && OFFGRID_PUBLIC_PORT="$PUBLIC_PORT" docker compose -f docker-compose.edge.yml up -d )
ok "Edge up on :$PUBLIC_PORT"

# ── 7. start the gateway on each gateway Mac (native) ─────────────────────────
hd "Gateway(s) — native Off Grid Desktop / headless gateway"
for gw in "${GATEWAYS[@]}"; do
  GW_CMD="OFFGRID_DATA_DIR=\$HOME/.offgrid OFFGRID_BIN_DIR=/opt/offgrid/bin OFFGRID_GATEWAY_PORT=$GW_PORT nohup npx @offgrid/gateway > \$HOME/offgrid-gw.log 2>&1 &"
  if [ "$gw" = "$CORE_IP" ]; then
    warn "Gateway is this Mac. Start it natively here (needs models + binaries):"
    say  "    $GW_CMD"
  else
    say "Starting gateway on $gw over SSH…"
    if ssh $SSH_OPTS "${SSH_USER}@${gw}" "bash -lc '$GW_CMD'" 2>/dev/null; then
      ok "  launched on $gw"
    else
      warn "  could not auto-start on $gw — SSH in and run the gateway manually (needs models/binaries)."
    fi
  fi
done

# ── 8. verify + report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
hd "Verify"
sleep 2
curl -fsS "http://localhost:$PUBLIC_PORT/healthz" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "edge → gateway /healthz reachable" \
  || warn "gateway /healthz not answering yet (start the native gateway; see above)."
curl -fsS "http://localhost:$PUBLIC_PORT/" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && ok "edge → console reachable" \
  || warn "console not answering yet (it may still be building/starting; see console.log)."

hd "Done"
say "${c_b}One URL for everyone on the WiFi:${c_0}  ${c_g}http://$CORE_IP:$PUBLIC_PORT${c_0}"
say "Tip: give the Macs stable names/IPs (DHCP reservation or .local) so the URL never moves."
